# idl1

> A desktop application for recording, storing and analysing motorcycle and
> bicycle suspension telemetry. A Rust engine (`idl-rs`) does every
> computation; a Tauri + TypeScript front end draws it. The unit of work is a
> **workbook**: a Markdown file with fenced `math`, `table`, `js` and prose
> cells, evaluated against a recorded session.

The three ideas worth knowing before reading anything else:

- **The workbook is a file; the app is a live viewer of it.** Editing a
  workbook in a text editor is a first-class way to use this software.
- **Rust computes, JavaScript draws.** No number the app depends on is
  computed in the front end, and no chart is drawn in Rust.
- **Log files and blobs are immutable.** A session's `data.parquet` is a pure
  function of its blob and the importer version; the catalog is a disposable
  index, never a source.

## Writing workbooks

- [Workbook reference](WORKBOOK-REFERENCE.md): every math builtin with its
  signature, unit rule, value shape and an example; the definition
  annotations; the JavaScript host variables; and the chart grammar the
  Properties panel reads and writes. Generated in part from the engine, so it
  cannot drift from what the engine does.

## Contracts

These are normative. Where a contract and any other document disagree, the
contract wins.

- [C1 — session schema](superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-idl1-c1-session-schema.md):
  what a session is on disk, including the unit and timestamp rules.
- [C2 — workbook v3](superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-idl1-c2-workbook-v3.md): the
  workbook container, the cell kinds, the maths language, the JavaScript
  runtime, and the merge semantics.
- [C3 — IPC surface](superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-idl1-c3-ipc-surface.md):
  every command the front end may call, its arguments, its return shape and
  its error rows.
- [C4 — data directory](superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-idl1-c4-data-directory.md):
  the layout of a library on disk, the atomic-write primitive, and the
  verification and repair checks.

## The device and the wire

- [IDL0 specification](IDL0_SPEC.md): the on-device log format and the
  device/host wire protocol. Parts 1–2 and §3–10 are current.
- [Signal pipeline](signal_pipeline.md): what happens to a sample between the
  sensor and a chart.

## Working on the code

- [Architecture](superpowers/specs/2026-09-02-idl1-rewrite-design.md): the
  layering, and which crate a given change belongs in.
- [CI](CI.md): what runs on a push, what is manual, and why.
- [Releasing](RELEASING.md): how an installer is built and published.

## Using the library from a terminal

`AGENTS.md` is written at the root of every idl1 library and describes that
library's own folders, the CLI verbs with an example each, and the rules about
what must never be edited. Read it before touching a library's files.

## Optional

- [Design rationale](design_rationale.md): why the engine computes what it
  computes, for the suspension physics rather than the software.
- [Hardware setup](HARDWARE_M10_SETUP.md): wiring and sensor placement.
